title: Two Skeletons: A Hunter and a Farmer. Who Lived Better?
desc:
One skeleton is tall with clean joints. The other has cavities and a worn spine. Most people guess wrong about which one was the farmer.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: Farming Made Humans Shorter by Up to 15 cm
desc:
In parts of Greece and Turkey, men's average height fell by around fifteen centimetres after farming arrived, and took thousands of years to come back.
Full video on our YouTube channel.

title: Hunter-Gatherers Found Food in 15 Hours a Week
desc:
In 1963 Richard Lee timed the Ju/'hoansi in the Kalahari. Finding food took adults about 15 hours a week. You pass that by Tuesday afternoon.
Watch the full story on our YouTube channel.

title: Did Ancient Humans Really Work Less Than You?
desc:
The fair answer: 15 hours was food only. Add tools, cooking and chores and it was nearer 40. But no commute, no boss, no fixed shift.
Full video on our YouTube channel.

title: Humans Hunted by Running Animals Into Exhaustion
desc:
We sweat and keep cooling while moving. Four-legged runners have to stop and pant. Track one long enough in the heat and it can't run again.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: The Original Morning Meeting, 50,000 Years Ago
desc:
Leftovers by the fire, and a quick chat about where the water is good and who saw fresh tracks. That was the whole plan for the day.
Full video on our YouTube channel.

title: People Made Jewellery Long Before Money Existed
desc:
At Blombos Cave in South Africa, archaeologists found shell beads about 75,000 years old, each one drilled by hand. Not to eat. Just to look good.
Watch the full story on our YouTube channel.

title: A 40,000-Year-Old Flute Made From a Vulture's Bone
desc:
In 2008, researchers in Hohle Fels cave in Germany pieced together a flute with five finger holes. Someone in the Ice Age had time to learn to play it.
Full video on our YouTube channel.

title: Before Insurance, Your Friends Were Your Safety Net
desc:
No money, no police, no hospital. If your hunt failed or you broke a leg, only other people could keep you alive. Friendship was survival.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: What Did Ancient Humans Talk About Around the Fire?
desc:
In daytime talk it was food, tracks and gossip. By the fire, 81% of long conversations were stories: ancestors, how the world began, people far away.
Full story on our YouTube channel.

title: Waking Up at 2 AM Might Not Be a Disorder
desc:
Old European records describe a 'first sleep' and a 'second sleep' with a waking hour between. Not every study agrees, but your body may be doing something very old.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.

title: Farming Looked Like an Upgrade. It Was a Loop
desc:
More food meant more children. More people needed more food. More fields meant more work, every season, every year.
Full video on our YouTube channel.

title: Once Farming Started, There Was No Going Back
desc:
When a village grew too big to live off wild food, the door shut. Ploughing, sowing, weeding, harvesting, guarding, forever.
Watch the full story on our YouTube channel.

title: When Did Your Hours Start Belonging to Someone Else?
desc:
Villages became towns, towns became cities, and something new arrived: hours sold in exchange for food you no longer knew how to find.
Full video on our YouTube channel.

title: They Were Already Standing on the Finish Line
desc:
We chase retirement to finally get our time back. For most of human history, afternoons went to craft and friends, and nights went to stories.
Watch the full video on our YouTube channel.
